summary: A large, mountainous botanical garden in Mae Rim, with themed glasshouses, a canopy walk, trails, a rose garden and a natural science museum. Its spread-out layout makes this a substantial half-day outing.
whyGo: See tropical and specialised plant collections, including the rainforest glasshouse, amid a wooded mountain setting.
Combine the elevated Canopy Walks with easier greenhouse and museum visits; the official garden lists multiple distinct areas and trails.
bestFor: Plant lovers, families and travellers wanting a nature-focused break from Chiang Mai city.
Visitors with a car or a prearranged driver who can explore a large site at their own pace.
skipIf: You need step-free access throughout or cannot manage uneven paths; access conditions for each attraction are not clearly documented.
You have only a short city stop and no transport plan for the Mae Rim area.
duration: Allow 3–5 hours as a planning estimate for the canopy walk and a selection of glasshouses or trails; a thorough visit can take longer.
cost: The Botanic Gardens Organization announced rates effective 1 October 2026: foreign adults ฿250, foreign children ฿150; Thai adults ฿80, secondary students ฿50, and children aged 6–12 / primary pupils ฿20. The listed garden tour tram is ฿60 adult / ฿30 child. Vehicle-entry fees are not specified in this new notice, so check with the garden before driving in.
hours: Tourism Authority of Thailand lists daily opening 08:30–17:00. Recheck the garden's official channels before travel for December 2026 changes and last-entry times.
bestTime: Start in the morning for cooler walking and time to cover the distant attractions before closing. December is within Chiang Mai's drier, cooler season; glasshouses may still feel warm and humid.
gettingThere: The garden is in Mae Rim on the Mae Rim–Samoeng route. A private car or prearranged driver is the simplest option for the spread-out grounds; the garden's new tariff lists a tour tram inside the site. Public transport and return ride-hailing reliability were not confirmed in current official information.
booking: No advance booking requirement was found for general admission. Pay on arrival; contact the garden directly to confirm December hours, vehicle fees, tram operation and any group arrangements.
accessibility: The site is mountainous and includes trails and an elevated canopy walkway. Current official information reviewed does not specify step-free routes, wheelchair access, accessible transport or restroom provision at individual attractions; contact the garden about specific mobility needs.
practicalTips: Plan the order of stops before arrival and allow time to travel between areas; the official site lists Canopy Walks, greenhouse groups, Rose Garden, Natural Science Museum and several trails.
Wear shoes suitable for outdoor paths, carry water and sun protection, and bring a light layer for the cooler morning.
Keep cash available for incidental purchases and confirm which fees apply to your vehicle before setting out.
decemberNotes: December is a popular cool-season period, so expect more visitors than in the wet season, especially around holidays. The latest official Botanic Festival notice found was for 26 December 2025–4 January 2026; it does not establish the dates or programme for December 2026. The newly announced admission rates already apply by the research date.
uncertainties: The new official tariff notice lists admission and tram charges but does not state vehicle-entry fees; older third-party prices should not be relied on.
Confirm exact December 2026 opening and last-entry times, tram schedule, and any attraction closures directly with the garden.
No authoritative public-transport or detailed accessibility guidance was found.
